newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - U.S. data set to dominate.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - U.S. data set to dominate.

text.p: UK gilts will struggle for independence from mighty U.S. Treasuries this week as a glut of crucial U.S. data threatens to dominate world bond markets.
"There is so much important U.S. data out this week gilts will have to have an international focus, despite the monetary meeting," said Philip Shaw, group economist at Union Plc.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George meet for their monthly monetary policy discussion on Wednesday but gilts will have to wait until Friday for the week's main event, the U.S. October jobs report.
The voguish U.S. employment cost index for the third quarter on Tuesday and GDP on Wednesday will give it something to chew on in the meantime.
The cost index is due at 1330 GMT and forecast to show a 0.8 percent increase, the same rise it recorded in Q2.
A bigger number is likely to unsettle U.S. Treasuries and other bond markets and make them even more apprehensive about the rest of the week's data.
U.S. GDP growth is forecast to slow to 1.8 percent in the third quarter following growth of 4.7 percent in the second.
But the non-farm payroll is forecast to show a chunky monthly rise, up 212,000 in October after September's surprise 40,000 fall.
Long-dated gilts will be vulnerable to strong economic data and analysts said the 10-year area of the curve looks set to stay volatile for many months ahead.

The spread at 10 years between gilts and Bunds concertinaed out and in again last week as it was hit by mixed economic news. It stood at 170 basis points on Monday morning but many analysts see it as vulnerable at that level.

"The spread managed to get down to 155 basis points due to the wave of enthusiasm over EMU convergence, but given the Labour party's comments (on Monday) on Britain's entry, the market's enthusiasm is likely to wane," said Shaw.
Labour's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said in a newspaper interview on Monday that a Labour government may delay Britain's entry into EMU and said the obstacles were formidable.
Also on the home front, the monthly monetary meeting should offer gilts some more temporary domestic direction.
Most analysts expect rates to stay on hold at 5.75 percent after the meeting, but this outcome could encourage the short end to reconsider its pessimistic view on interest rates.
The short sterling strip is factoring in a quarter-point monetary tightening before the end of the year and a half point rise by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
This is at odds with the economic consensus which forecasts rates on hold until the second half, with the first rise coming after the general election which must be held by May 1997.

"The short end is still far too pessimistic. Sterling's strong appreciation in the last two months has not even been felt in the short sterling strip. The monetary meeting should help it rally a bit," said a salesman at a UK brokerage.
Sterling has appreciated by over six percent on a trade weighted basis since early August which is effectively a monetary tightening.

Traders are also hoping the authorities will iron out some oddities further along the yield curve. The seven-year area has been over-priced for a month or more and this kink could be promptly ironed out by a generous tap issue from the Bank.
"Yield curve models show the seven-year benchmark standing eight basis points through the par curve," said Steven Andrew, gilts analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"Similarly, the swap spread over this gilt is 10 basis points greater than for the rest of the curve between four and 10 years. We suspect the time for a correction has come."

The funding schedule suggests the Bank of England will not have the chance to sell 7-year stock at auction until January 1997. "But the Bank may have a convenient gap in its calendar to issue conventional stock via the tap method," said Andrew.
The funding remit states the Bank can only issue 10 percent of funding in taps, but so far it has sold just 600 million stg in the fiscal year against a limit of 3.4 billion stg.
